reply.english: Yesterday I went to the market.
I saw my aunt by chance.
Yes, I bought a new shirt.

phrases.arabic: أَوَّل مِبَارِح كَان عِنْدِي دَوَام لَحِتَّى الْمِسَا
phrases.transliteration: awwal mbeeri7 kan 3indi dawaam la7atta l-masa

reply.english: We stayed up until one o'clock.

reply.arabic: مَا قِدِرْت، كَان عِنْدِي شُغِل كِتِير
reply.english: I couldn't, I had a lot of work.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: مرحبا لينا، كيفك؟
dialogue.transliteration: mar7aba Lina, keefek?
dialogue.english: Hi Lina, how are you?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: أهلين رامي، منيحة الحمد لله. وينك كنت مبارح؟
dialogue.transliteration: ahleen Rami, mnii7a l7amdilla. wenak kint mbeeri7?
dialogue.english: Hi Rami, good thank God. Where were you yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: كنت بالشغل، كان عندي دوام لحتى المسا
dialogue.transliteration: kint besh-shughl, kan 3indi dawaam la7atta l-masa
dialogue.english: I was at work, I had a shift until the evening.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: يي، دوام طويل! أكلت غدا؟
dialogue.transliteration: yi, dawaam Taweel! akalt ghada?
dialogue.english: Wow, a long shift! Did you eat lunch?

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: لأ، ما كان في وقت. أكلت بس مسا بالبيت
dialogue.transliteration: la2, ma kan fi wa2it. akalt bas masa bil-beet
dialogue.english: No, there wasn't time. I only ate in the evening at home.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: مسكين! أنا رحت عالسوق مبارح واشتريت أغراض
dialogue.transliteration: miskeen! ana ru7et 3as-soo2 mbeeri7 w-ishtareet aghraaD
dialogue.english: Poor you! I went to the market yesterday and bought some things.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: شو اشتريتي؟
dialogue.transliteration: shu ishtareeti?
dialogue.english: What did you buy?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: اشتريت قمصان وشوية خضرة
dialogue.transliteration: ishtareet 2mSaan w-shwayet khuDra
dialogue.english: I bought some shirts and some vegetables.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: طيب، وبعدين شو عملتي؟
dialogue.transliteration: Tayyeb, w-ba3deen shu 3milti?
dialogue.english: Ok, and then what did you do?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: قعدت عند صحبتي شوي وشربنا قهوة
dialogue.transliteration: 2a3adet 3ind SaHebti shwayye w-shribna 2ahwe
dialogue.english: I sat at my friend's place a bit and we drank coffee.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: كتير حلو. أنا نمت بدري مبارح من التعب
dialogue.transliteration: kteer 7ilu. ana nimet badri mbeeri7 mnet-ta3ab
dialogue.english: Very nice. I slept early yesterday from tiredness.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: خد راحتك اليوم إذا فيك
dialogue.transliteration: khood ra7tak l-yom iza feek
dialogue.english: Take it easy today if you can.

response.english: I didn't do anything, I stayed at home.

pair.english: Where were you at seven o'clock yesterday?
Did you eat something good yesterday?

response.english: Yes, we cooked kibbeh and it was delicious.
It was quiet, I slept early.

lessons.culture: مبارح is the everyday Damascene word for yesterday; the MSA أمس sounds bookish and is rarely heard in casual talk. Asking شو عملت مبارح؟ is a normal way to open a catch-up conversation with a friend or neighbor.

exercises.prompt: صاحبك بيسألك: "مبارح شو عملت؟". جاوب إنك رحت عالسوق.

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA but far too formal for a casual catch-up; مبارح رحت عالسوق is what is actually said.

exercises.tip: "مبارح" replaces the MSA "أمس" in everyday speech.

exercises.prompt: بيسألوك: "وينك كنت مبارح بالليل؟". جاوب إنك كنت بالبيت.

too_formal.feedback: المنزل is a formal written word; Damascenes say البيت in speech.

exercises.tip: "بالبيت" = at home.

exercises.prompt: أكمل: "_____ كان يوم طويل." المعنى: Yesterday was a long day.

too_formal.feedback: أمس is the MSA word; in spoken Damascene the word is مبارح.

exercises.tip: "مبارح" opens the sentence, like "yesterday" in English.

exercises.prompt: أكمل: "تعبت كتير مبارح من _____." المعنى: I got very tired from work yesterday.

too_formal.feedback: العمل is correct but bookish; the everyday word for work is الشغل.

exercises.tip: "الشغل" is the word Damascenes use for work or a job.

exercises.prompt: ترجم: "What did you do yesterday?" (تحكي مع رجال)

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA, but شو not ماذا is how "what" is really said in Damascus.

exercises.tip: "شو" = what, used constantly in spoken Damascene.

exercises.prompt: ترجم: "Who did you see yesterday?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA; spoken Damascene uses مين for who and شفت for saw.

exercises.tip: "مين" = who.

exercises.prompt: أي جملة معناها "I bought a new shirt yesterday"؟

too_formal.feedback: Grammatically fine MSA, but البارحة and the case endings are not how this is said day to day.

exercises.tip: A past-tense verb plus مبارح marks something already done.

exercises.prompt: شو معنى "قديش سهرتوا مبارح؟"؟
exercises.answer: How late did you stay up yesterday?
accepted: How late did you stay up yesterday?
options: How late did you stay up yesterday?
exercises.tip: "سهر" = to stay up late, to have a late night.

exercises.prompt: رتب الجملة: مبارح كان الجو حلو كتير
exercises.tip: "الجو" = the weather.

exercises.prompt: رتب الجملة: تعبت كتير مبارح من الشغل
exercises.tip: "تعبت" = I got tired.

phrases.arabic: لَمَّا كِنْت صِغِير كِنْت أَحِبّ أِلْعِب بَرَّا
phrases.transliteration: lamma kint zghir kint ba7ibb el3ab barra

phrases.arabic: كِلّ صِيف كِنَّا نِرُوح عِنْد جِدِّي بِالْقَرْيَة
phrases.transliteration: kell Seef kinna nrou7 3ind jiddi bel-2arye

phrases.arabic: جِدِّتِي كَانِت تِحْكِيلِنَا حِكَايَات قِبْل النَّوْم
أَوَّل دِرَّاجَة كَان عِنْدِي كَانِت حِمْرَا
كِنْت أَخَاف مِنْ الظَّلَام كِتِير لَمَّا كِنْت صِغِير
phrases.transliteration: kint khaayef mnel-Zalaam kteer lamma kint zghir

phrases.arabic: كِنَّا نِمْشِي عَالْمِدْرَسَة سَوَا كِلّ يَوْم
لَمَّا كِنْت صِغِير حِلِمْت إِنِّي صِير طَيَّار
phrases.transliteration: lamma kint zghir 7lemet inni Seer Tayyar

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: هنا، بتفتكري بيتكم القديم؟
dialogue.transliteration: Hana, bteftikri beetkon el2adeem?
dialogue.english: Hana, do you remember your old house?

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.arabic: أكيد بفتكر، تربيت فيه لحتى عمري عشر سنين
dialogue.transliteration: akeed baftikir, trabbayt feeh la7atta 3omri 3ashr sneen
dialogue.english: Of course I remember, I grew up in it until I was ten.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: كنتي تلعبي شو بالحارة؟
dialogue.transliteration: kintii tel3abi shu bel-7aara?
dialogue.english: What did you use to play in the alley?

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.arabic: كنا نلعب استغماية مع ولاد الجيران
dialogue.transliteration: kinna nel3ab estoghmaaye ma3 wlaad ij-jeeraan
dialogue.english: We used to play hide and seek with the neighbors' kids.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: وأنا كنت ألعب كرة قدم كل مسا
dialogue.transliteration: w-ana kint el3ab kurt 2adam kell masa
dialogue.english: And I used to play soccer every evening.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.arabic: بتفتكر أستاذك بالمدرسة الابتدائية؟
dialogue.transliteration: btiftikir ostaazak bel-madrase l-ebtida2iyye?
dialogue.english: Do you remember your teacher in elementary school?

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: إي، كان اسمه أستاذ فؤاد وكان صارم كتير
dialogue.transliteration: ee, kan ismo ostaaz Fu2ad w-kan Saarim kteer
dialogue.english: Yes, his name was Ustaz Fu2ad and he was very strict.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.arabic: هاها، أستاذتي كانت لطيفة، كانت تعطينا حلويات
dialogue.transliteration: haha, ostaazti kanet laTeefe, kanet ta3Teena 7alawiyyaat
dialogue.english: Haha, my teacher was nice, she used to give us sweets.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: زمان كنا نمشي عالمدرسة، هلق كل شي بالسيارة
dialogue.transliteration: zamaan kinna nemshi 3al-madrase, halla2 kell shi bes-sayyaara
dialogue.english: Back then we walked to school, now everything is by car.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.arabic: صحيح، الحياة كانت أبسط بكتير
dialogue.transliteration: Sa7ee7, el-7ayaat kanet absaT b-kteer
dialogue.english: True, life was much simpler.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: بفتكر أول دراجة كان عندي، كانت حمرا وكنت أحبها كتير
dialogue.transliteration: baftikir awwal drraaje kan 3indi, kanet 7amra w-kint ba7ebba kteer
dialogue.english: I remember my first bike, it was red and I loved it so much.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.arabic: يا زمان! هلق ولادنا حتى ما بيعرفوا هالألعاب
dialogue.transliteration: ya zamaan! halla2 wladna 7atta ma bi3rafo hal-al3aab
dialogue.english: Oh those days! Now our kids don't even know these games.

response.english: I grew up in old Damascus.

pair.arabic: شو كنتوا تلعبوا لما كنتوا صغار؟
pair.transliteration: shu kintu tel3abu lamma kintu zghaar?
pair.english: What did you use to play when you were kids?

response.english: We used to play hide and seek and soccer.

pair.english: Who used to tell you stories?

response.english: My grandmother used to tell us every night.

pair.arabic: شو كان حلمك لما كنت صغير؟
pair.english: What was your dream when you were young?

response.english: My dream was to become a pilot.

lessons.culture: Grandparents' houses, especially in villages outside Damascus, are where extended families still gather in the summer. Children of that generation played in the street or alley (الحارة) rather than indoors, and adults often speak of that time as simpler and safer.

exercises.prompt: صاحبك بيسألك: "وين تربيت؟". جاوب إنك تربيت بدمشق.

too_formal.feedback: نشأت is literary MSA; the spoken verb for grew up is تربيت.

exercises.tip: "تربيت" = I grew up, I was raised.

exercises.prompt: بيسألوك: "شو كان حلمك لما كنت صغير؟". جاوب إنه كان حلمك تصير طيار.

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA, but إني صير is the natural spoken way to say "that I become".

exercises.tip: "صير" = become, used constantly in spoken Damascene for future roles.

exercises.prompt: أكمل: "كنا _____ كرة قدم بالحارة." المعنى: We used to play soccer in the alley.

too_formal.feedback: نلهو is a literary word for playing; everyday speech uses نلعب.

exercises.tip: "كنا" plus a present-tense verb marks a habitual past action.

exercises.prompt: أكمل: "جدتي كانت _____ حكايات قبل النوم." المعنى: My grandmother used to tell us stories before sleeping.

too_formal.feedback: تروي fits written narration; تحكيلنا is how it is really said.

exercises.tip: "تحكي" plus لـ plus a pronoun means "tell someone".

exercises.prompt: ترجم: "I had a friend named Kareem."

too_formal.feedback: لدي and يُدعى are formal written Arabic; spoken Damascene uses عندي and اسمه.

exercises.tip: "عندي" = I had/have; "اسمه" = his name (is).

exercises.prompt: ترجم: "We used to walk to school together."

too_formal.item: كنا نذهب إلى المدرسة سوياً مشياً
too_formal.feedback: Technically correct but stiff; نمشي عالمدرسة سوا is the natural spoken version.

exercises.tip: "عالمدرسة" = to school (على plus المدرسة contracted).

exercises.prompt: أي جملة معناها "Back then life was much simpler"؟

too_formal.item: كانت الحياة في الماضي أبسط بكثير
too_formal.feedback: Correct but bookish; زمان is how Damascenes say "back then".

exercises.tip: "زمان" opens a sentence about the past, like "back then".

exercises.prompt: شو معنى "كنت أخاف من الظلام كتير"؟
exercises.answer: I used to be very afraid of the dark
accepted: I used to be very afraid of the dark
options: I used to be very afraid of the dark
I used to love the dark
I am afraid of loud noises
I used to play in the dark
exercises.tip: "أخاف من" = to be afraid of.

exercises.prompt: رتب الجملة: كل صيف كنا نروح عند جدي
exercises.answer: كل صيف كنا نروح عند جدي
accepted: كل صيف كنا نروح عند جدي
exercises.tip: "عند" = at (someone's place).

exercises.prompt: رتب الجملة: أول دراجة كان عندي كانت حمرا
exercises.answer: أَوَّل دِرَّاجَة كَان عِنْدِي كَانِت حِمْرَا
accepted: أَوَّل دِرَّاجَة كَان عِنْدِي كَانِت حِمْرَا
exercises.tip: "حمرا" = red, matching the feminine دراجة.

dialogue.speaker: Yara
dialogue.arabic: فادي، شكلك زعلان، شو صار؟
dialogue.transliteration: Fadi, shaklak za3laan, shu Saar?
dialogue.english: Fadi, you look upset, what happened?

dialogue.speaker: Fadi
dialogue.arabic: لا تسألي، يوم أسود اليوم
dialogue.transliteration: la tis2ali, yom aswad il-yom
dialogue.english: Don't ask, a black day today.

dialogue.speaker: Yara
dialogue.arabic: ليش، شو صار بالضبط؟
dialogue.transliteration: leesh, shu Saar beD-DabT?
dialogue.english: Why, what exactly happened?

dialogue.speaker: Fadi
dialogue.arabic: الصبح تأخرت عن الشغل، وبعدين ضاع مفتاح السيارة مني
dialogue.transliteration: iS-Sob7 it2akhkharet 3an ish-shughl, w-ba3deen Da3 miftaa7 is-sayyaara minni
dialogue.english: This morning I was late for work, and then I lost my car key.

dialogue.speaker: Yara
dialogue.arabic: يي حرام! لقيته؟
dialogue.transliteration: yi 7araam! la2eeto?
dialogue.english: Oh no! Did you find it?

dialogue.speaker: Fadi
dialogue.arabic: إي، لقيته تحت الكنبة بعد ساعة دوران
dialogue.transliteration: ee, la2eeto ta7t il-kanabe ba3d saa3a dawaraan
dialogue.english: Yes, I found it under the couch after an hour of searching.

dialogue.speaker: Yara
dialogue.arabic: طيب، وبعدين شو صار؟
dialogue.transliteration: Tayyeb, w-ba3deen shu Saar?
dialogue.english: Ok, and then what happened?

dialogue.speaker: Fadi
dialogue.arabic: وأنا رايح عالشغل خربت السيارة بنص الطريق
dialogue.transliteration: w-ana rayye7 3ash-shughl kharbet is-sayyaara b-noSS iT-Taree2
dialogue.english: And while I was heading to work, the car broke down in the middle of the road.

dialogue.speaker: Yara
dialogue.arabic: لا! وشو عملت؟
dialogue.transliteration: la2! w-shu 3milt?
dialogue.english: No! And what did you do?

dialogue.speaker: Fadi
dialogue.arabic: اتصلت بالكراج وانتظرت نص ساعة عالشارع
dialogue.transliteration: ittaSalet bel-garaaj w-intaZaret nuSS saa3a 3ash-shaare3
dialogue.english: I called the garage and waited half an hour on the street.

dialogue.speaker: Yara
dialogue.arabic: مسكين، يوم تعبان فعلا
dialogue.transliteration: miskeen, yom ta3baan fi3lan
dialogue.english: Poor you, a really exhausting day.

dialogue.speaker: Fadi
dialogue.arabic: إي، بس الحمد لله خلص وما صار شي أكبر
dialogue.transliteration: ee, bas il7amdella khilis w-ma Saar shi akbar
dialogue.english: Yes, but thank God it's over and nothing worse happened.

response.english: I lost my key and was late for work.
My phone broke and I lost all my pictures.

pair.english: How did the car break down?

response.arabic: ما بعرف، وقفت لحالها بنص الطريق
response.transliteration: ma ba3rif, wi2fet la7alla b-noSS iT-Taree2
response.english: I don't know, it just stopped by itself in the middle of the road.

pair.english: Did you find the lost bag?

response.arabic: لأ، لسا عم يفتشوا عليها بالمطار
response.english: No, they're still searching for it at the airport.

lessons.culture: يوم أسود (a black day) is how Damascenes describe a day where everything goes wrong, and حرام is said as a sympathetic exclamation, not a religious judgment, when someone tells you their bad news.

exercises.prompt: صديقتك بتسألك: "شو صار معك؟". جاوب إنه ضاع مفتاحك.

too_formal.feedback: فقدت is correct MSA but sounds like a report; spoken Damascene says ضاع مفتاحي.

exercises.tip: Damascene often makes the object get lost (ضاع) rather than saying "I lost it".

exercises.prompt: بيسألوك: "ليش شكلك متضايق؟". جاوب إنه انكسر تلفونك.

too_formal.feedback: تحطّم and هاتف are formal written words; the spoken words are انكسر and تلفون.

exercises.tip: "تلفون" is the everyday word for phone in Damascene, not "هاتف".

exercises.prompt: أكمل: "_____ الكهربا كل الليل." المعنى: The power went out all night.

too_formal.feedback: انطفأت fits a light going out, not the whole power supply; انقطعت الكهربا is the phrase used.

exercises.tip: "انقطعت الكهربا" is the fixed phrase for a power outage.

exercises.prompt: أكمل: "وقعت عالدرج و_____ رجلي." المعنى: I fell on the stairs and hurt my leg.

too_formal.feedback: أصبت is correct MSA for got injured; spoken Damascene says ضربت رجلي for hurt my leg.

exercises.tip: "ضربت" here means hurt/hit a body part, not only "hit someone".

exercises.prompt: ترجم: "I was late for work this morning."

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA, but الشغل and هالصبح are the spoken forms of work and this morning.

exercises.tip: "هالصبح" = this morning, a spoken contraction of هذا الصبح.

exercises.prompt: ترجم: "The car broke down in the middle of the road."

too_formal.feedback: Correct but formal; spoken Damascene uses خربت and بنص الطريق.

exercises.tip: "خربت" = broke down, of a machine or a car.

exercises.prompt: أي جملة معناها "I forgot my wallet at home"؟

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA; بالبيت is the everyday form of at home.

exercises.tip: "نسيت" = I forgot.

exercises.prompt: شو معنى "انسكب القهوة عاللابتوب تبعي"؟
options: I spilled coffee on the floor
exercises.tip: "انسكب" = spilled, something spilled by itself.

exercises.prompt: رتب الجملة: نمت وما سمعت المنبه
exercises.tip: "ما سمعت" = I didn't hear.

exercises.prompt: رتب الجملة: جرحت إيدي وأنا بطبخ
exercises.tip: "وأنا بطبخ" = while I was cooking.

phrases.arabic: قَالُولِي إِنْكِن رَح تِنْتِقِلُوا عَبِيت جِدِيد
عِمّ يِحْكُوا إِنُّه الْمِحَلّ الْفِلَانِي سِكِّر
لِسَّا مَا تَأَكَّدْنَا، مِمْكِن تِكُون إِشَاعَة بِس
phrases.transliteration: lissa ma t2akkadna, mumkin tkoon eshaa3a bas

phrases.arabic: مَا تِصْدِّق شُو صَار مِبَارِح بِالْحَارَة
phrases.transliteration: ma tSaddi2 shu Saar mbeeri7 bel-7aara

reply.arabic: وَلَا شِي جِدِيد، كِلّ شِي تَمَام
reply.transliteration: wala shi jdeed, kell shi tamaam

phrases.arabic: لَا تِحْكِيلْحِدَا، بِس سِمِعْت إِنُّه رَح يِسَافِرُوا
phrases.transliteration: la ti7killa7ada, bas sme3et inno ra7 ysaafro

phrases.arabic: هاد كله كلام ناس، ما بعرف صحيح ولا لأ
phrases.transliteration: had kello klaam naas, ma ba3rif Sa7ee7 wala la2

dialogue.speaker: Rasha
dialogue.arabic: نور، ما بتصدقي شو سمعت!
dialogue.transliteration: Nour, ma btSaddi2i shu sme3et!
dialogue.english: Nour, you won't believe what I heard!

dialogue.speaker: Nour
dialogue.arabic: شو في؟ قوليلي بسرعة
dialogue.transliteration: shu fi? 2ooleeli bi-sur3a
dialogue.english: What is it? Tell me quickly.

dialogue.speaker: Rasha
dialogue.arabic: سمعت إنه سامر ولينا خطبوا
dialogue.transliteration: sme3et inno Samer w-Lina khaTabo
dialogue.english: I heard that Samer and Lina got engaged.

dialogue.speaker: Nour
dialogue.arabic: لا! جد؟ مين قلك؟
dialogue.transliteration: la2! jadd? meen 2allek?
dialogue.english: No! Really? Who told you?

dialogue.speaker: Rasha
dialogue.arabic: أختي شافتن سوا بالمطعم وبعدين قالتلي جارتنا الخبر
dialogue.transliteration: ekhti shaafton sawa bel-mat3am w-ba3deen 2altilli jaartna l-khabar
dialogue.english: My sister saw them together at the restaurant, and then our neighbor told me the news.

dialogue.speaker: Nour
dialogue.arabic: يي، ما كنت أتوقع! وامتى العرس؟
dialogue.transliteration: yi, ma kint atwa22a3! w-imta l-3irs?
dialogue.english: Wow, I didn't expect that! And when is the wedding?

dialogue.speaker: Rasha
dialogue.arabic: لسا ما حددوا، بس رح يحكوا لأهلهن هالأسبوع
dialogue.transliteration: lissa ma 7addado, bas ra7 ye7ku la-ahlon hal-osboo3
dialogue.english: They haven't set a date yet, but they'll tell their families this week.

dialogue.speaker: Nour
dialogue.arabic: طيب لا تحكي لحدا لحتى يعلنوا هني
dialogue.transliteration: Tayyeb la ti7ki la7ada la7atta y3linu honi
dialogue.english: Ok don't tell anyone until they announce it themselves.

dialogue.speaker: Rasha
dialogue.arabic: أكيد، بيني وبينك بس
dialogue.transliteration: akeed, beini w-beinek bas
dialogue.english: Of course, just between us.

dialogue.speaker: Nour
dialogue.arabic: وشو صار مع المحل يلي كان جنب بيتك؟ سمعت إنه سكر
dialogue.transliteration: w-shu Saar ma3 il-ma7all yalli kan jamb beetek? sme3et inno sakkar
dialogue.english: And what happened with the shop that was next to your house? I heard it closed.

dialogue.speaker: Rasha
dialogue.arabic: إي، سكر من شهرين، بس ما بعرف ليش بالضبط
dialogue.transliteration: ee, sakkar min shahrein, bas ma ba3rif leesh beD-DabT
dialogue.english: Yes, it closed two months ago, but I don't know exactly why.

dialogue.speaker: Nour
dialogue.arabic: خسارة، كان محل حلو
dialogue.transliteration: khsaara, kan ma7all 7ilu
dialogue.english: What a shame, it was a nice shop.

pair.english: Who told you they're getting married?

response.english: My friend, and she heard it from their family.

pair.english: Is this talk true or a rumor?

response.english: I don't know, but that's what I heard.

response.arabic: ولا شي مهم، كل شي عادي

lessons.culture: Neighborhood news travels fast by word of mouth in Damascus, and a phrase like لا تحكيلحدا (don't tell anyone) is said as a normal part of sharing gossip, not really expected to be kept secret. An unconfirmed rumor is often softened with هاد كلام ناس, that's just people talking.

exercises.prompt: صحبتك بتسألك: "مين قلك هالخبر؟". جاوب إنه صحبتك قالتلك.

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA, but قالتلي is the everyday spoken verb for told me.

exercises.tip: "قالتلي" = she told me (قالت plus لي).

exercises.prompt: بيسألوك: "شو آخر الأخبار عندك؟". جاوب إنه ما في شي جديد.

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA but sounds like a formal statement; ولا شي جديد is the relaxed spoken answer.

exercises.tip: "ولا شي" = nothing, not a single thing.

exercises.prompt: أكمل: "سمعت _____ سامر خطب." المعنى: I heard that Samer got engaged.

too_formal.feedback: أنّ is the MSA conjunction; spoken Damascene uses إنه after verbs like سمعت.

exercises.tip: "سمعت إنه..." = I heard that..., a fixed spoken pattern.

exercises.prompt: أكمل: "ممكن تكون _____ بس." المعنى: It might just be a rumor.

too_formal.feedback: شائعة is the standard written spelling; spoken Damascene says إشاعة.

exercises.tip: "إشاعة" = rumor.

exercises.prompt: ترجم: "Who told you this news?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA; spoken Damascene says مين قلك instead of من أخبرك.

exercises.tip: "قلك" = told you (قال plus لك).

exercises.prompt: ترجم: "You won't believe what happened yesterday."

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA, but spoken Damascene uses ما تصدق and شو صار instead.

exercises.tip: "ما تصدق" = you won't believe, literally you don't believe.

exercises.prompt: أي جملة معناها "My sister got married last month"؟

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA word order; spoken Damascene usually puts the subject first: أختي جوزت.

exercises.tip: "جوزت" = got married, said of a woman.

exercises.prompt: شو معنى "هاد كله كلام ناس"؟
exercises.tip: "كلام ناس" = gossip, unverified talk.

exercises.prompt: رتب الجملة: سمعنا إنهن رزقوا بصبي
exercises.tip: "رزقوا بصبي" = they were blessed with a baby boy, a fixed expression.

exercises.prompt: رتب الجملة: لا تحكيلحدا بس سمعت إنه رح يسافروا
exercises.answer: لا تحكيلحدا بس سمعت إنه رح يسافروا
accepted: لا تحكيلحدا بس سمعت إنه رح يسافروا
exercises.tip: "لا تحكيلحدا" = don't tell anyone.

challenge.title: Tell Me What Happened
challenge.instructions: Write and say a short Damascene conversation that lasts at least 10 lines, between two people catching up. It must include asking what happened yesterday, an answer using past tense, a childhood memory, one thing that went wrong, and one piece of news or gossip you heard. Use at least 8 target phrases from Unit 16 and include both a masculine-address form and a feminine-address form.
required_elements: A question about yesterday using مبارح and شو عملت or شو صار.
An answer describing something that happened, using a past-tense verb.
A memory from childhood using لما كنت صغير or كنا.
Something that went wrong, using a word like انكسر, ضاع, or تأخرت.
A piece of news or gossip introduced with سمعت إنه or قالولي.
At least one masculine-address form such as كنت or شفت.
At least one feminine-address form such as كنتي or شفتي.
A closing reaction such as يي، حرام، or مسكين.

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: ميسا، كيفك؟ شو عملتي مبارح؟
dialogue.transliteration: Maysa, keefek? shu 3milti mbeeri7?
dialogue.english: Maysa, how are you? What did you do yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: Mayssa
dialogue.arabic: أهلين بلال، ما تصدق شو صار معي مبارح!
dialogue.transliteration: ahleen Bilal, ma tSaddi2 shu Saar ma3i mbeeri7!
dialogue.english: Hi Bilal, you won't believe what happened to me yesterday!

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: شو في؟ قوليلي!
dialogue.transliteration: shu fi? 2ooleeli!
dialogue.english: What is it? Tell me!

dialogue.speaker: Mayssa
dialogue.arabic: انكسر تلفوني وضاع مفتاح البيت مني بنفس اليوم
dialogue.transliteration: inkasar talifoni w-Da3 miftaa7 il-beet minni b-nafs il-yom
dialogue.english: My phone broke and I lost the house key on the same day.

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: يي حرام! هيك يوم بيفكرني بلما كنت صغير، كنا نضيع كل شي!
dialogue.transliteration: yi 7araam! heik yom byfakkirni b-lamma kint zghir, kinna nDay3e2 kell shi!
dialogue.english: Oh no! A day like that reminds me of when I was young, we used to lose everything!

dialogue.speaker: Mayssa
dialogue.arabic: ههه صحيح! بس خلص لقيت المفتاح آخرتها
dialogue.transliteration: hehe Sa7ee7! bas khilis la2eet il-miftaa7 aakhirta
dialogue.english: Haha true! But in the end I found the key eventually.

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: طيب الحمد لله. بالمناسبة، سمعت إنه سامر خطب
dialogue.transliteration: Tayyeb il7amdella. bel-munaasabe, sme3et inno Samer khaTab
dialogue.english: Good, thank God. By the way, I heard Samer got engaged.

dialogue.speaker: Mayssa
dialogue.arabic: لا! جد؟ مين قلك؟
dialogue.transliteration: la2! jadd? meen 2allek?
dialogue.english: No! Really? Who told you?

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: صحبتي قالتلي، بس لسا ما تأكدت
dialogue.transliteration: SaHebti 2altilli, bas lissa ma t2akkadet
dialogue.english: My friend told me, but I haven't confirmed it yet.

dialogue.speaker: Mayssa
dialogue.arabic: يا سلام، خبر حلو إذا صحيح. مسكين شفت شو صار معك اليوم
dialogue.transliteration: ya salaam, khabar 7ilu iza Sa7ee7. miskeen shuft shu Saar ma3ak il-yom
dialogue.english: Wonderful, nice news if it's true. Poor you, look what happened to you today.

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: هيك هي الحياة، يوم أسود ويوم حلو
dialogue.transliteration: heik hiyye l-7ayaat, yom aswad w-yom 7ilu
dialogue.english: That's life, a black day and a nice day.
